title: Tell HN: Google Play will public-share your address and phone if you sell in EU
summary:
tl;dr (quoted from the email, full below):

* If you are an individual developer declared as a trader, provide and verify a public phone number. Please be aware that your phone number and address will be displayed publicly on Google Play.

* You’re typically considered a trader under European Economic Area (EEA) and United Kingdom (UK) laws if you engage in commercial activities, including when you earn revenue from your apps (such as paid downloads, in-app products, subscriptions, or ads).

* If you don't complete your trader status declaration by the deadline, you won't be able to submit app updates, and your developer profile and all apps will be removed from Google Play globally.

* You must declare your trader status in Play Console, regardless of where you’re located.

Email from Google Play received 7 hours ago:

Hi ,

Updated Google Play policies now require you to declare whether you’re a trader or non-trader in Play Console.

What you need to know

You must declare your trader status in Play Console, regardless of where you’re located.

You’re typically considered a trader under European Economic Area (EEA) and United Kingdom (UK) laws if you engage in commercial activities, including when you earn revenue from your apps (such as paid downloads, in-app products, subscriptions, or ads). If you operate purely as a hobbyist or in a non-commercial capacity, you can declare as a non-trader.

If you don’t distribute apps in the EEA or UK, you can declare as a non-trader.

What this means for you

You must complete your trader status declaration in Google Play Console by February 1, 2027:

Declare your trader status

1. Sign in to Google Play Console.

2. Go to Manage account > Account details > About you.

3. Under Trader status, select Declare your trader status and choose whether you are a trader or non-trader.

4. If you are an individual developer declared as a trader, provide and verify a public phone number. Please be aware that your phone number and address will be displayed publicly on Google Play.

5. If you declare as a trader, certify commitment to compliance with local laws.

6. Review your profile details and click Save.

If you don't complete your trader status declaration by the deadline, you won't be able to submit app updates, and your developer profile and all apps will be removed from Google Play globally.

Also documented here: https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/17594752

title: Ask HN: Is it possible for a residential proxy provider to exist ethically?
summary:
I'm leaning towards "no", because I've not seen a single bulk residential proxy provider that doesn't use some form of trickery to get people to agree to a TOS/AUP that bundles their proxy. Extremely few if any users install a residential proxy allowing unknown 3rd parties to run traffic through their house with full knowledge of what that really means, nor are they compensated for it.

title: Binance hack> need better software integrity verification
summary:
The binance hack exposed a worsening issue with standards around software integrity verification. Code signing and integrity verification has fallen short for today's needs.

Package managers usually verify checksums during install, but this fails against upstream supply chain attacks or post-install mods. There needs to be a more widely adopted mechanism or standard for continuous verification of installed tooling against a source of truth. This applies to scripts and compiled binaries, with the latter being more challenging when built locally from variable inputs.

title: Tell HN: Codex Ultrafast is slower than Fast
summary:
I could generate a nice sloppy website hyping up my claims with all kinds of graphs, but I hope HN will forgive me for a brief human-written post. Although token streaming is faster, response latency is significantly higher. This response latency is incurred with every sub-turn, tool call, etc, and ends up completely negating the token generation speed. On short and long tasks alike, Fast achieves task completion faster than Ultrafast. I lit $500 on fire to discover this, so I thought it might be helpful to warn others not to do the same.

title: Ask HN: Fable 5.1 or Opus 5.5?
summary:

It seems like people only talk about Opus and never Fable anymore. I myself use Fable since it's supposed to be better or more powerful.

When I run multiple versions of a technical task and have Fable choose the best one blind, Fable itself always picks the Opus one. This may be due to the tendency of Opus to probe deeper and work longer (producing more evidence) though.

It feels like there is a big hole right now where Fable 5.5 should be. Opus 5.5 seems to work and explain better, yet it's supposedly limited compared to Fable.

title: Ask HN: Is it possible the field's course gets readjusted to normalcy again?
summary:
There's been an influx of slop, and working hasn't been as fun as it was; however, I was thinking if, perhaps, this is all happening because we're in a transition and it's not final, and maybe we're not gonna die.

I'm sorry if that sounds young-ish; I'm not a veteran, though I've been trying to be a bit more hopeful towards the future, but what if in the near future, the slop gets more filtered, and there are more job openings for things that are fun, and different skills flourish in the AI era, and writing specs becomes the thing we get our kicks out of.

It's dreadful for me that we don't need to 'write' code anymore, still, I have faith there'll be fun things in the future.
